title.narrative: Share-Net Bangladesh

description.narrative: Share-Net Bangladesh is the country hub of Share-Net International, a Knowledge Platform focusing on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR). Share-Net Bangladesh is the first of Share-Net International’s country hub, drawing on the years of experiences and interventions by practitioners, researchers, and policymakers in the field of sexual reproductive health, especially placing SRHR at the centre of human rights. Share-Net Bangladesh aims to bring together the Communities of Practice (CoP) that consist of social and medical researchers, development practitioners, health workers, government officials and legal experts to engage with one another to find solutions and take critical issues forward. Share-Net Bangladesh is hosted by RedOrange Media and Communications. Priorities of Share-Net Bangladesh: * Promote interaction between the national, international, sustainable and empowered community of practice and encourage them to share learning. * To apply the knowledge to evidence-informed SRHR programs, policies and practices. * Enable the members and the strategic partners to connect, discuss, share, translate and jointly operate this knowledge network on SRHR. * Ensure the accessibility of the policymakers, practitioners and researchers to the knowledge platform and enable them to address the relevant knowledge gaps on SRHR scientifically, politically and practically (Language: English)

comment.narrative: A qualitative exploration on how women and adolescents are suffering in coastal Bangladesh due to climate change and sea level rise induced salinity intrusion.International Centre for Diarrhoea Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b)The menstrual needs and challenges of marginalised communities are often overlooked and left out when we discuss the challenges and development needs of these communities, resulting in a phenomenon we term as 'marginalisation inside marginalisation'. This phenomenon is leading to rising menstrual inequity inside the country and we aim to combat this issue in our project through research and policy advocacy. We have selected four marginalised communities with unique menstrual needs and challenges inside Bangladesh- brothel-based sex-workers, bede (nomadic community), tea garden workers, and visually impaired individuals for this project. We want to create a research report that documents the menstrual practices, needs, and challenges of these communities and use the findings from the report to prepare a policy brief addressing the menstrual inequity they face. We will disseminate the report and policy brief in a policy advocacy roundtable discussion where we along with selected representatives from the marginalised communities will advocate for policy reforms, research, and action for menstrual equity to relevant policymakers, development practitioners, and researchers. We will also raise public awareness on ensuring menstrual equity of marginalised communities through a comprehensive social media campaign.Deliverable: Research ReportGive Bangladesh Foundation Uncharted Red Waters: Exploring Menstrual Equity of Selected Marginalised Communities in Bangladesh Through Policy and ActionThe menstrual needs and challenges of marginalised communities are often overlooked and left out when we discuss the challenges and development needs of these communities, resulting in a phenomenon we term as 'marginalisation inside marginalisation'. comment.narrative: ●Share-Net Bangladesh Knowledge Fair Introductory Video ●Share-Net Bangladesh Knowledge Fair Infographic Video●Share-Net Bangladesh Regional Conference Introductory Video●Share-Net Bangladesh Knowledge Fair Post-Conference Video ●Share-Net Bangladesh Regional Conference Post-Conference VideoShare-Net Bangladesh Knowledge Fair Introductory Video: In one-word youth was the main spirit of the video. Youth have been at the forefront of many global movements, fighting injustice and calling for democratic reforms in Bangladesh. Bangladesh has an opportunity to address systemic and structural issues of governance, rule of law and human rights. Bangladesh's youth are agents of change. Their engagement is essential to uphold democratic values and ensuring that future development is underpinned by equity, non-discrimination and social justice. Now is the time to harness the energy and creativity of Generation Z and ensure that Bangladesh fulfils its enormous potential. Share-Net Bangladesh Knowledge Fair Infographic Video: This video showed that youth-led movement that places SRHR at the center of Bangladesh's development and highlighted different years Knowledge Fair and different types of plenary sessions, parallel discussions, and regional collaborations. This video encouraged people from different sectors to know that the Knowledge Fair will provide a unique opportunity for stakeholders to come together, share insights, and co-create solutions that are informed by the experiences and aspirations of young people. Share-Net Bangladesh Regional Conference Introductory Video: The interface of youth must be broadened to engage young people who remain underrepresented, such as youth from remote rural areas, young women, persons with disabilities, religious minorities, gender and sexual minorities, and those from ethnic minority communities.Challenges such as limited access to comprehensive sexual education, widespread gender-based violence, and insufficient platforms for youth leadership continue to hinder their ability to fully exercise their rights. Without a conscious effort to bring unheard voices to influence change, the status quo will continue. Building the capabilities of youth is important so they can better articulate and influence policies. This is applicable for any country specially the neighboring country and for Bangladesh itself. In this video we showed how through a series of discussions SNBD is planning to build the foundations of an inclusive and people-centered SRHR system in different aspects in which young people have a greater stake in the country's development. This Video showed how each session is bringing together participants from Bangladesh, Nepal, India, and Pakistan to share knowledge and best practices on integrating SRHR through promoting youth leadership.

comment.narrative: The thematic Communities of Practice (CoPs) form the backbone of Share-Net Bangladesh’s activities. Till now Share-Net has set up 9 CoPs. In 2024, eight CoPs will be reconvened in 2024 , focusing on a wide range of SRHR-related topics. The purpose of the meeting will be to check in with the CoP members and see how they can take the CoP agenda forward without Share-Net Bangladesh’s facilitation going forward. The meetings facilitated dialogue, knowledge exchange, and collaboration among stakeholders, enhancing the capacity of members to advance SRHR advocacy and implementation across different sectors.1.CoP on Climate Change and SRHR (9 members, another 16 members from SHIRIM activities)2.CoP on SRHR and Education (17 members) In 2024, the CoP topics were aligned with the overall thematic topic for Share-Net Bangladesh, so the CoPs can contribute to other activities also so other activities can contribute to CoPs. The CoP Climate Change was merged with SHIRIM National Learning Session Activities, so the CoP meetings went year-round simultaneously with SHIRIM activities. The CoP SRHR and Education was merged with the annual Knowledge Fair theme and the knowledge product from this CoP was used as the Keynote presentation for the Knowledge Fair. Therefore the CoP work continued simultaneously with Knowledge Fair activities. The meetings were facilitated and coordinated by Samiul Islam, CoP Facilitator and Knowledge Management Expert. In addition, on 29 October 2024, Share-Net Bangladesh (SNBD) convened an in-person Community of Practice (CoP) Members’ Meeting, where around 25 members representing our 9 CoPs actively participated. The meeting provided a valuable platform for reflection, exchange of ideas, and discussion on the future direction of the CoPs.During the session, members shared their commitment to continue this collaborative approach within their respective organisations, ensuring that the learnings and practices of the CoPs are embedded into broader institutional work. Recognising that many of the CoP members now hold senior managerial positions with expanded responsibilities and limited time, they proposed engaging younger and newer members to sustain and strengthen this initiative. Senior members pledged to provide supervision and monitoring, thereby ensuring continuity while creating opportunities for the next generation of CoP leaders.Reflections and Insights from Members:●Future Goals: Members highlighted the need for policy influence, increased awareness, and stronger community engagement as key objectives for the coming years.●Community Engagement: Suggestions were made to prioritise marginalised groups and underrepresented regions to deepen outreach efforts.●Collaboration: Participants emphasised building stronger partnerships with government bodies, NGOs, and grassroots organisations to enhance collective impact.●Measuring Success: Proposed indicators included improved access to knowledge resources, visible policy impact, and strengthened community networks.●Capacity Building: Members expressed the need for training in policy advocacy, digital tools, and innovative communication strategies.●Innovation: Ideas such as using digital platforms, storytelling, and interactive knowledge-sharing tools were identified as ways to increase impact.●Challenges: Limited funding, time constraints, and difficulties in sustaining engagement were mentioned as recurring obstacles.●Sustainability: Members recognised the importance of long-term funding strategies, structured mentoring, and institutionalising knowledge-sharing practices.To facilitate ongoing collaboration, SNBD is planning to introduce a separate communication method (such as a group chat or online portal) where CoP members can connect, exchange updates, and share knowledge independently of formal meetings.The meeting reaffirmed the strengths of the CoPs—such as strong partnerships, collective knowledge, and dedication of members—while also underlining the importance of innovation and sustainability to ensure long-term impact.

comment.narrative: Share-Net Bangladesh 9TH SRHR Knowledge Fair 2024Share-Net Bangladesh is proud to organise the 9th SRHR Knowledge Fair in 2024, a flagship event that continues to champion knowledge sharing and collaboration in the field of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR). The 2020 Share-Net Bangladesh (SNBD) Knowledge Fair marked a key moment in advancing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) for young people in Bangladesh. The 5th edition of this annual event, held virtually, introduced the theme "Youth Power" for the first time, focusing on the role of youth in shaping SRHR. This event brought together a wide range of participants, including practitioners, activists, researchers, policymakers, and young people, to discuss SRHR issues affecting adolescents and youth. Since the 2020 Knowledge Fair, young people in Bangladesh have taken the lead in pushing for improvements in SRHR, using what they learned to advocate for change. Specially, in recent times, we have seen youths taking part in a great national reformation movement. As SNBD prepares for the 9th SRHR Knowledge Fair in 2024, "Youth Power” aims to build on these efforts, empowering youth to continue driving positive change in SRHR, ensuring their rights and well-being remain a priority. Bangladesh, a nation with a huge youth population, stands at a pivotal juncture where the engagement of young people in the SRHR discourse is not just desirable but essential. The country’s youth, comprising 47 million people aged 15-29, as noted in the National Youth Policy 2017, represent a significant demographic with the potential to drive sustainable development and social change. The theme of the event "YouthPower 2024: Nothing Without Us," emphasised that youth themselves will take the lead, positioning those who support them at the forefront. By doing so, we recognise that young people are the driving force behind the SRHR movement in Bangladesh. They will guide the discussions and shape the policies that impact their lives. Around 350 experts, academicians, and experienced professionals from various development organisations, along with high-ranking Government officials and foreign delegates have joined this day-long conference. Throughout the event, the discussants and research presenters tried to showcase the latest innovations, information and relevant facts by analysing the intersection of SRHR-Youth Power from an international perspective, as well as from urban and rural perspectives.The 9th SRHR Knowledge Fair was presented with academic partner Asian University of Women to inspire Youth Power. Also, the Chief of Health, United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Bangladesh, Dr. Vibhavendra Raghuvanshi, extended invaluable support and guidance to Share-Net Bangladesh throughout the conference.He said in his The whole event was organised by Red Orange Communications, the host organisation of Share-Net in Bangladesh.His Hines Mr. Thijs Woudstra, Deputy Head of Mission, Embassy of Kingdom of Netherlands joined as special guest and stated that It is essential to recognise that young people should not just be participants but leaders in shaping their own Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) journey. They must have a seat at the table where decisions affecting their lives are made. All youth, regardless of gender, background, or socioeconomic status, should have equitable access to SRHR services and education .He will ensure that marginalised voices are heard and included in policy-making.Md. Saifullahil Azam, Director General, Directorate General of Family Planning was the chief guest of the event and stated that DGFP, under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, is committed to ensuring the successful implementation of the "National Strategy for Adolescent Health 2017-2030" developed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. By aligning services with this comprehensive strategy, they aim to enhance the sexual and reproductive health rights (SRHR) of youth and adolescents, ensuring access to essential information and services across Bangladesh. He also said that they will focus on delivering youth-friendly SRHR services through community clinics, outreach programs, and family planning centers. Our aim is to provide accessible and confidential SRHR services, particularly for marginalised and vulnerable youth, ensuring no one is left behind, in line with SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and SDG 5 (Gender Equality).This year's Knowledge Fair featured a diverse range of sessions, discussions, and presentations focusing on integrating SRHR for youth It provided a platform for experts and stakeholders to share innovative approaches, research findings, and success stories in the fields of SRHR for the youth. The event was attended by a mix of government officials, academicians, healthcare professionals, members of civil society, students from different educational institutions and international delegates.The fair ended by presenting the Share-Net SRHR Recognition Award 2024 in three categories: the 'Youth Leadership Award' was given to Tajkia Mariam Jahan – Youth:, a youth leader working for SERAC Bangladesh ; the 'Community Champion Award' was given to Ms .Julia Ahmed, an independent consultant and public health Expert; and the 'Lifetime Achievement Recognition' was given to Dr. Yasmin , independent consultant and Former Vice President and Senior Regional Director of Marie Stopes Headquarter in London, for her tremendous contribution in the field of SRHR.Among the other prominent guests present at the event were, Dr. Bernd Spanier, Deputy Head of Delegation, EU Delegation to Bangladesh, Biplob Barua Line Director (FP - FSD) Field Services Delivery Unit, Directorate General of Family Planning, Dr. Mohammad Zahirul Islam, Health Advisor, Development Cooperation Section, Embassy of Sweden in Bangladesh, Dr. Mohiuddin Ahsanul Kabir Chowdhury, Assistant Professor, Dept. of Public Health, Asian University for Women (AUW) , Professor Dr. Abu Naser Zafar Ullah, Vice Chancellor, RTM Al-Kabir Technical University , Mahmuda Sultana, Programme Director, Oxfam in Bangladesh , Dr. Sushmita Ahmed, Senior Advisor (Partnership and Coordination), Ipas Bangladesh, S M Saikat, Executive Director, SERAC and many more. The knowledge fair was live broadcasted online and further detail can be found in the below link - https://www.youtube.com/@share-netbangladesh6730/streams News Report: 1.The Business Standard2.Daily Business Eye3.BSS News4.Daily Kalbela5.Daily Ittefaq 6.The Daily Star 7.Deepto News 8.Jamuna News
